title: Self-serve analytics query builder and cost drilldown paths for enterprise consoles
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers frequently request ad-hoc exports and bespoke cost breakdowns (per-team, per-route, per-model) but often can't assemble them without engineering support. This creates backlog pressure on the data team and slows customer onboarding for Reserved/Dedicated customers.

Proposal: Build a self-serve analytics query-builder in the Redwood Console that lets workspace admins and billing owners compose, preview, and persist ad-hoc exports and standardized "Cost Drilldown" templates. Key capabilities:
- Visual query builder for common dimensions (workspace, tenant, route, model, deployment mode, token ranges, date windows) with prebuilt filters for SLA and cost anomalies.
- Template library: shareable cost drilldown templates (e.g., daily per-workspace spend, 30-day per-model avg token cost, burst events by route) that can be cloned and customized.
- Export targets: CSV, Parquet (S3 integration for enterprise), and scheduled email delivery.
- Permission model: admin and billing roles control who can create templates and schedule exports; viewers can run/preview.
- Cost-sensitive sampling: when large time windows requested, system suggests sampling or preview to prevent expensive ad-hoc runs.

Why now: Several mid-market and enterprise customers (sales pipeline) cited this as a gating factor for Dedicated adoption and for demonstrating cost transparency in procurement. Solves operational load on Data/Support and improves self-serve monetization flows.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Full raw-query power vs safe templated UX: we prioritize templates and composable visual filters first, deferring an advanced SQL console behind an opt-in enterprise flag to reduce support and data-exposure risk.
- Query cost control: need quotas/sampling to avoid runaway queries; will reuse telemetry/scheduler work from PM-70321 for throttles.
- RBAC complexity: we must integrate with existing SSO/SAML and workspace roles; scope limited to console RBAC for MVP.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Console UI for building queries with at least 8 common dimensions and start/end dates.
2) Template library with 5 built-in templates (cost by workspace, 30d per-model avg, token density by route, daily aggregate tokens, reserved vs hosted split).
3) Exports: ad-hoc CSV download and scheduled S3 (Parquet) export for enterprise tenants with encryption-at-rest option.
4) Sampling suggestion visible when estimated row count or time range exceeds threshold and an opt-in full-run available for admins.
5) Permission enforcement validated in prod-like test workspace and documented for Security review.

Rollout plan:
- Alpha: Internal + 3 pilot enterprise customers (support + AE cohort) — telemetry and feedback.
- Beta: opt-in in customer consoles, release feature flag, add S3 configuration for enterprise.
- GA: default in Console, monitored quotas and SLAs.

Dependencies: PM-70321 (throttles/quota gating), PM-61234 (export orchestration), ENG-1842 (RBAC integration for console), DES-98 (template UX pattern).
